script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Garden of Forgiveness

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

MRS. JENKINS (40s), a woman with salt-and-pepper hair, stands at the kitchen counter. She slices a cucumber, the juicy green skin hitting the cutting board. Her husband, MR. JENKINS (50s), sits at the table, staring at his coffee.

MRS. JENKINS
(looking at her husband)
You're quiet this morning. Everything okay?

MR. JENKINS
(sighs, looks up)
Just...thinking.

MRS. JENKINS sets the cucumber on the cutting board and sits across from her husband.

MRS. JENKINS
About what?

MR. JENKINS
Work. The new project. I've been having some...issues.

MRS. JENKINS reaches across the table and takes her husband's hand.

MRS. JENKINS
We'll work it out, sweetheart. But first, let me make you a sandwich.

INT. LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON

MR. JENKINS sits on the couch, staring at an empty photo frame. Wife and two children smile back at him. A knock on the door interrupts his thoughts. He stands to answer it.

MR. JENKINS (cont'd)
(opens door)
Hi, Mr. and Mrs. Thompson.

MR. THOMPSON (50s) and MRS. THOMPSON (40s) stand at the door, their younger son, TOMMY (8), clutching a bouquet of flowers.

MR. JENKINS
(surprised)
Tommy! I didn't know you were coming over.

MRS. THOMPSON
We thought we'd surprise you. We wanted to apologize for what happened at the park.

MR. JENKINS
(nods)
Accepted. And thank you for the flowers.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

MRS. JENKINS washes the dishes while MR. JENKINS helps their daughter, EMMA (10), with her homework.

MR. JENKINS
(looking at his wife)
You know, today was a good day.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
Why's that?

MR. JENKINS
I ran into the Thompsons, and we talked. We forgave each other for something that happened years ago.

MRS. JENKINS
That's wonderful, dear.

INT. GARDEN - MORNING

The sun rises over the garden, illuminating the flowers. MR. JENKINS and MR. THOMPSON work together, planting new flowers in the garden.

MR. JENKINS
You know, this garden is a symbol of our friendship. It represents growth and forgiveness.

MR. THOMPSON
(smiling)
I couldn't agree more.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

MRS. JENKINS, MR. JENKINS, EMMA, and TOMMY sit at the table, sharing a meal.

EMMA
Dad, can we invite the Thompsons over again?

MR. JENKINS
(smiling)
Of course, honey.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

MR. JENKINS and MRS. JENKINS sit on the couch, enjoying a quiet moment together.

MRS. JENKINS
You know, I'm glad we were able to forgive the Thompsons.

MR. JENKINS
(looking at his wife)
Me too. Forgiveness is a powerful thing.

MRS. JENKINS leans her head on her husband's shoulder.

MRS. JENKINS
It's also a gift. And we have the power to give it to others.

MR. JENKINS
(smiling)
And to receive it.

INT. GARDEN - NIGHT

Under the light of the moon, MR. JENKINS and MR. THOMPSON tend to the garden, their friendship stronger than ever. The camera pans out, revealing the beautiful, thriving garden, a symbol of growth, forgiveness, and the power of human connection.

THE END
